## Historical audit — S0116

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r2/sceneevolve_cli/C1/test/commons_163096530/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 2 of 3 is available; citations below identify its JSONL lines and supplied character ranges.

| Evidence | Observation |
|---|---|
| Goal and scene, line 15 `model_request` [0,160331) | The explicit task was an editable, separate-mesh reconstruction of one indoor RGB image, matching camera, geometry, placement, occlusion and materials. The student's inferred scene was a historic dormitory: code constructs architecture, three bunk assets, a wardrobe, fireplace, heater, bucket and clock. These names and estimated image anchors are not independent confirmation of reference contents. |
| Construction and connections, lines 15 and 18 `execute` [0,10942) | The programs group multiple primitive meshes into assets, including bunk posts, rails, ladders and bedding. Grouping and endpoint coordinates show intended connections, not verified physical contact or absence of intersections. No human pose is established; the code specifies furniture placements and orientations. Separate colors, metal settings and procedural wood noise/bump are implemented, but their rendered appearance is not independently visible here. |
| Autonomous iteration, line 15 | Harness feedback reports steps 1 and 2 successful and supplies render paths. After step 1, the student claimed left bunks needed larger silhouettes and repositioning, the right bunk needed edge cropping, and floor/iron needed darker materials. The second program changed placement, camera/lens, lighting and materials. These are student diagnoses, not independently verified image differences. |
| Final revision, lines 17 `model_response` [0,10293) and 18 | The student estimated the rear junction was 15 pixels too low, the fireplace lintel too low, and the nearest bunk too narrow with tall posts. The executed revision lowered camera target height, raised the fireplace surround, widened the near bunk and shortened left bunk posts. The pixel estimate is a claim, not a supplied measurement. |
| Validation and selection, line 19 `execution_result` [0,73044); lines 20–21 `select` [0,59) each | Step 3 reports `ok: true`, a finished 16-sample render, saved image and blend file, and empty stderr; step 3 is selected twice. This establishes technical build/render success and selection, not visual or geometric correctness. The visible excerpt contains no subsequent student critique of step 3. |
| Input and constraints, lines 15–16 `codex_session` [0,3825) | The visible request contains system procedure and harness render feedback, but no identifiable teacher diagnosis, proposed update or teacher message; therefore teacher receipt and adoption are unsubstantiated. The third student session reports zero tool calls; its staged inputs include the reference and two renders. No external exploration is evidenced. |

**Outcome and uncertainty:** Formal execution succeeded for all three reported builds; final reconstruction correctness remains unknown. The actual images are not visible in this audit, so object count in the reference, part contact, pose, camera match, lighting, occlusion, texture quality and render defects cannot be independently assessed. No algorithm failure, empty patch or technical interruption is shown in this excerpt. A transferable procedural lesson is to distinguish global camera changes from local geometry changes and validate after rendering; this case attempted both, but whether its particular bunk and fireplace corrections improved the match remains an unresolved hypothesis.
